title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 156 (Effect of mixture, without bailor’s consent, when the goods can be separated)

content.overview: Section 156 provides that if the bailee, without the consent of the bailor, mixes the goods of the bailor with his own goods and the goods can be separated or divided, the property in the goods remains in the parties respectively; but the bailee is bound to bear the expense of separation or division, and any damage arising from the mixture. The statutory illustration concerns marked bales of cotton.
content.glance: Non-consensual mixture that can be separated leaves property in the respective parties; the bailee bears the cost of separation and any damage from the mixture.
content.study: If the bailee, without the consent of the bailor, mixes the goods of the bailor with his own goods and the goods can be separated or divided, the property in the goods remains in the parties respectively; but the bailee is bound to bear the expense of separation or division, and any damage arising from the mixture. Illustration: A bails 100 bales of cotton marked with a particular mark to B. B, without A’s consent, mixes them with his own differently marked bales. A is entitled to have his 100 bales returned, and B must bear the expense of separation and any incidental damage. Current-law framing: separability preserves distinct ownership but shifts separation costs and mixture damage to the bailee.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: If the bailee, without the consent of the bailor, mixes the goods of the bailor with his own goods and the goods can be separated or divided, the property in the goods remains in the parties respectively; but the bailee is bound to bear the expense of separation or division, and any damage arising from the mixture.

sections.heading: Statutory illustration
sections.body: A bails 100 bales of cotton marked with a particular mark to B. B, without A’s consent, mixes the 100 bales with other bales of his own, bearing a different mark. A is entitled to have his 100 bales returned, and B is bound to bear all the expenses incurred in the separation of the bales, and any other incidental damage.

examples.title: Separable non-consensual mixture
examples.body: Marked bales mixed without consent can be separated. Property remains with the respective owners; bailee bears separation costs and any mixture damage under Section 156.

hypotheticals.question: Bailee mixes the bailor’s goods with his own without consent, but the goods can be separated. What is the result?
hypotheticals.analysis: Under Section 156 property remains in the parties respectively, but the bailee must bear the expense of separation and any damage arising from the mixture.
